title: 노인 단백질 섭취, 많이 드시면 근육과 걸음이 지켜질까요?
description: 노인 단백질 섭취와 근육, 연구에서는 어땠을까요? 11,332명 연구에서 단백질을 넉넉히 드신 분의 힘과 걸음이 좋았지만, 오래 지켜보면 운동이 함께여야 했어요.
image_alt: 노인 단백질 섭취와 함께 걷기를 이어 가듯 숲길을 나란히 걷는 밀짚모자 쓴 노부부의 뒷모습을 그린 수채화
image_prompt: Watercolor illustration of an elderly couple in straw hats walking side by side on a shaded pine forest path, seen from behind.
body_markdown:
명절에 뵌 어머니의 팔이 예전보다 가늘어 보여서, 돌아오는 길 내내 마음에 걸리셨던 적이 있나요. "요즘은 입맛이 없어서 밥에 김치만 먹는다"는 말씀을 들으면 고기라도 더 챙겨 드려야 하나 싶어집니다. 노인 단백질 섭취가 정말 근육과 걸음을 지켜 주는지, 연구가 알려 준 것을 차근차근 정리해 볼게요.

한눈에 보는 답부터 말씀드릴게요. 평균 나이 75세 무렵 어르신 11,332명을 살핀 연구들에서는 권장량보다 단백질을 더 드시는 분들이 다리 힘, 손아귀 힘, 균형, 걷는 속도가 더 좋은 쪽으로 관련이 있었어요 [2]. 하지만 평균 85세 무렵 어르신 12,424명을 오래 지켜본 연구에서는 단백질을 많이 드신다고 해서 손아귀 힘이나 걷는 속도가 덜 줄지는 않았어요 [2]. 노인 단백질 섭취는 중요하지만, 근육을 지키려면 몸을 쓰는 운동이 함께 가야 한다는 뜻이에요.

## 노인 단백질 섭취, 많이 드시면 근육이 더 단단할까요?

한 시점에 여러 어르신을 비교해 보면, 단백질을 넉넉히 드시는 분들의 몸 기능 점수가 더 높았어요 [2]. 이 연구는 동네에 사시는 분, 병원에 계신 분, 운동을 꾸준히 해 온 분까지 22편의 연구를 모아 살폈어요 [2]. 다리 힘과 손아귀 힘, 균형 잡기까지 여러 가지가 함께 좋은 쪽으로 나타났어요 [2]. 다만 한 번에 비교한 연구는 "단백질을 드셔서 튼튼해졌다"인지 "튼튼한 분이 잘 드신다"인지를 가려 주지 못해요. 입맛과 기운이 함께 좋은 분일수록 잘 드시는 것일 수도 있어요. 그래도 잘 드시는 것과 몸의 힘이 함께 간다는 점은 분명히 눈여겨볼 만해요. 부모님 식사가 부쩍 줄었다면 그 자체가 살펴볼 신호일 수 있어요.

## 오래 지켜보면 결과가 달라질까요?

9편의 연구에서 어르신들을 여러 해 지켜본 결과는 조금 달랐어요 [2]. 권장량보다 단백질을 많이 드신 분들도 손아귀 힘과 걷는 속도가 줄어드는 속도는 비슷했어요 [2]. 연구진은 단백질을 많이 먹는 것만으로는 시간이 지나며 몸 기능이 줄어드는 것을 막는다고 보기 어렵다고 정리했어요 [2]. 그러니 밥상만 바꾸고 안심하기보다, 몸을 움직이는 습관을 함께 챙기는 것이 중요해요. 음식은 근육의 재료이고, 운동은 그 재료를 근육으로 쓰게 하는 신호라고 생각하시면 쉬워요.

## 근육을 지키는 데는 어떤 운동이 맞을까요?

근육이 줄어드는 근감소증 어르신 1,252명이 참여한 23편의 연구를 모아 보니, 운동은 손아귀 힘, 무릎 펴는 힘, 다리 근육량, 걷는 속도를 좋아지게 했어요 [1]. 특히 근력 운동과 여러 운동을 섞은 운동은 근육의 힘을 키웠지만, 걷기 같은 유산소 운동만으로는 근력이 뚜렷이 늘지 않았어요 [1]. 연구진은 여럿이 함께, 지도를 받으며 하는 근력 운동을 권했어요 [1]. 걷기는 그대로 이어 가시되, 의자에서 일어났다 앉기 같은 다리 근력 운동을 곁들이시면 좋아요. 다만 운동을 해도 팔 근육량이나 몸 전체 근육량은 뚜렷이 늘지 않았다고 하니, 눈에 보이는 굵기보다 힘과 걸음이 나아지는지를 살펴보세요 [1]. 계단을 오르실 때 덜 힘들어하시는지, 장바구니를 드는 손이 덜 떨리는지가 좋은 기준이 되어 줘요.

## 운동과 영양을 함께 챙기면 어떤 차이가 있을까요?

이탈리아에서 근감소증이 있는 큰 간 수술 환자 60명을 살핀 연구가 있어요 [4]. 수술을 기다리는 6주 동안 매일 걷기, 일주일에 두 번 병원에서 지도받는 운동, 영양 보충을 함께 한 쪽은 수술 뒤 합병증이 13.3%로, 평소처럼 지낸 쪽의 50%보다 낮았어요 [4]. 근육량과 근력도 운동과 영양을 함께 챙긴 쪽에서만 좋아졌어요 [4]. 수술을 앞둔 분들의 연구이지만, 운동과 먹는 것을 함께 챙길 때 몸이 달라질 수 있다는 점을 보여 줘요. 한 가지만 열심히 하는 것보다 두 가지를 조금씩 함께 하는 편이 낫다는 이야기이기도 해요. 부모님이 스스로 장을 보고, 스스로 걸어 나가실 수 있는 하루를 오래 지키는 것이 우리가 바라는 모습이에요.

## 자주 묻는 질문

**Q. 생선 기름 영양제를 드시면 근육에 도움이 되나요?**
10편의 연구를 모은 분석에서 근육량과 일어나 걷는 검사에 작은 도움이 있었다고 해요 [5]. 효과가 크지 않아서, 영양제를 드실지는 담당 의사나 약사와 먼저 상의하시는 것이 좋아요.

**Q. 걷기만 해도 근감소증에 충분할까요?**
연구에서는 유산소 운동만으로는 근력이 뚜렷이 늘지 않았어요 [1]. 세계보건기구도 65세 이상 어르신께 근력 운동을 일주일에 2일 이상 하시길 권해요 [6].

**Q. 단백질은 하루에 얼마나 드셔야 하나요?**
알맞은 양은 몸무게와 콩팥 건강 등에 따라 달라서, 이 글의 자료로는 정확히 말씀드리기 어려워요. 콩팥 질환이 있으시면 꼭 담당 의사와 상의해 주세요.

## 오늘 해 볼 작은 걸음

노인 단백질 섭취는 운동과 짝을 이룰 때 더 의미가 있어요. 오늘 부모님과 이렇게 해 보세요.

- 끼니마다 달걀, 두부, 생선, 살코기 가운데 하나를 한 가지씩 곁들이기
- 식사 뒤 10분 걷기와 함께 의자에서 일어났다 앉기를 천천히 몇 번 해 보기
- 전화할 때 "오늘 단백질 반찬은 뭐 드셨어요?"라고 다정하게 여쭤보기

sources.title: Efficacy of Exercise on Muscle Function and Physical Performance in Older Adults with Sarcopenia: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
sources.journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
sources.text: This study aimed to analyze the efficacy of exercise interventions on muscle strength, muscle mass, and physical performance in older adults with sarcopenia. Randomized controlled studies assessing exercise effects on sarcopenia were searched in Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane Library, ProQuest, EBSCOhost, Scopus, EMBASE, and VIP and CNKI up to 31 March 2022. Data were expressed as weighted/standardized mean difference (MD/SMD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). I2 index was employed for heterogeneity. The initial search identified 5379 studies, and 23 studies involving 1252 participants met the inclusion criteria for further analysis. Results revealed that exercise interventions can significantly improve grip strength (MD = 2.38, 95%CI = 1.33-3.43), knee extension strength (SMD = 0.50, 95%CI = 0.36-0.64), muscle mass of lower extremities (MD = 0.28, 95%CI = 0.01-0.56), walking speed (SMD = 0.88, 95%CI = 0.49-1.27), and functional mobility (MD = -1.77, 95%CI = -2.11--1.42) among older adults with sarcopenia. No significant exercise effects were found on fat-free muscle mass, appendicular muscle mass, skeletal muscle mass, and muscle mass of the upper extremities. The results of subgroup analysis indicated that both resistance training and multicomponent exercise could significantly increase the muscle strength, while aerobic exercise did not. The findings suggest that exercise intervention can effectively improve muscle function and physical performance in older adults with sarcopenia, but has limited effects on the muscle mass of the upper extremities. In addition, it is highly recommended to apply group-based and supervised resistance training and multicomponent exercise in the prevention and treatment of sarcopenia among the older population.

sources.title: Protein intake and physical function in older adults: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
sources.text: BACKGROUND: The present study explored cross-sectional and longitudinal associations between protein intake and physical function in older adults. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of cross-sectional and longitudinal studies that investigated the association between protein intake and measures of physical function in older adults. Cross-sectional, case-control, and longitudinal cohort studies that investigated the association between protein intake and physical function as a primary or secondary outcome in people aged 60 + years were included. Studies published in languages other than English, Italian, Portuguese, or Spanish were excluded. Studies were retrieved from MEDLINE, SCOPUS, EMBASE, CINAHL, AgeLine, and Food Science Source databases through January 31, 2022. A pooled effect size was calculated based on standard mean differences (SMD), MD, log odds ratio (OR) and Z-score.. RESULTS: Twenty-two cross-sectional studies examined a total of 11,332 community-dwellers, hospitalized older adults, and elite senior athletes with a mean age of approximately 75 years. The pooled analysis indicated that a protein intake higher than the recommended dietary allowance (RDA) was significantly associated with higher Short Physical Performance Battery (SPPB) scores (SMD: 0.63, 95% CI: 0.27, 0.99, P-value: 0.0006), faster walking speed, greater lower-limb (SMD: 0.22, 95% CI: 0.04, 0.40, P-value: 0.02) and isometric handgrip strength (Z-score: 0.087, 95% CI: 0.046-0.128, P-value: 0.0001), and better balance (SMD: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.05, 0.62, P-value: 0.02). Nine longitudinal studies investigated 12,424 community-dwelling and native older adults with a mean age of approximately 85 years. A protein intake higher than the current RDA was not associated with lower decline in either isometric handgrip strength (logOR: 0.99, 95% CI: 0.97-1.02, P-value= 0.67) or walking speed (logOR: 0.92, 95% CI: 0.77-1.10, P-value= 0.35). CONCLUSIONS: A protein intake higher than the RDA is cross-sectionally associated with better physical performance and greater muscle strength in older adults. However, a high consumption of proteins does not seem to prevent physical function decline over time.

sources.title: Preserving Mobility in Older Adults with Physical Frailty and Sarcopenia: Opportunities, Challenges, and Recommendations for Physical Activity Interventions.
sources.text: One of the most widely conserved hallmarks of aging is a decline in functional capabilities. Mobility loss is particularly burdensome due to its association with negative health outcomes, loss of independence and disability, and the heavy impact on quality of life. Recently, a new condition, physical frailty and sarcopenia, has been proposed to define a critical stage in the disabling cascade. Physical frailty and sarcopenia are characterized by weakness, slowness, and reduced muscle mass, yet with preserved ability to move independently. One of the strategies that have shown some benefits in combatting mobility loss and its consequences for older adults is physical activity. Here, we describe the opportunities and challenges for the development of physical activity interventions in people with physical frailty and sarcopenia. The aim of this article is to review age-related physio(patho)logical changes that impact mobility in old age and to provide recommendations and procedures in accordance with the available literature.

sources.title: Prehabilitation With Exercise and Nutrition to Reduce Morbidity of Major Hepatectomy in Patients With Sarcopenia: The PREHEP Randomized Clinical Trial.
sources.text: IMPORTANCE: Sarcopenia is an emerging predictor of complications after liver surgery. Strategies to mitigate its impact are crucial to improving postoperative outcomes. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a 6-week multimodal prehabilitation program combining physical exercise and nutritional support reduces postoperative morbidity in patients with sarcopenia who are undergoing major hepatectomy. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This study is a single-center, open-label, randomized clinical trial conducted from April 2022 to January 2025. Adult patients with sarcopenia scheduled for major liver resection and requiring future liver remnant hypertrophy were randomized (1:1) to receive either structured prehabilitation or standard care. The trial was conducted in a tertiary hepatobiliary referral center in Italy. Enrolled adult patients had radiologically and functionally confirmed sarcopenia. Most patients underwent portal vein embolization and right hepatectomy. INTERVENTIONS: The intervention group received a 6-week program while awaiting future liver remnant hypertrophy including daily walking, supervised biweekly in-hospital exercise, and branched-chain amino acid and immune nutritional supplementation. The control group received standard perioperative care. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was 90-day postoperative morbidity, assessed by Clavien-Dindo classification. RESULTS: A total of 70 adult patients with radiologically and functionally confirmed sarcopenia were enrolled, and 60 (median [IQR] age, 69 [63-75] years; 32 male [53.3%]) were included in the final analysis. Most patients (52 [86.7%]) underwent portal vein embolization, and 63 (88.3%) underwent right hepatectomy. Overall morbidity was significantly lower in the prehabilitation group (4 of 30 [13.3%] vs 15 of 30 [50%]; odds ratio, 0.15; 95% CI, 0.04-0.55; P = .004), with an absolute risk reduction of 36.7% and number needed to treat of 3. All major complications occurred in the control group (6 of 30 [20%]; d = 0.40; P = .02). Muscle mass and strength improved significantly only in the prehabilitation arm. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this randomized clinical trial reveal that a 6-week structured prehabilitation program significantly reduced postoperative morbidity in patients with sarcopenia undergoing major liver resection. These findings support integrating exercise and nutritional interventions into preoperative care for high-risk surgical patients to improve surgical outcomes. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05281211.

sources.title: Effects of Omega-3 Fatty Acids on Muscle Mass, Muscle Strength and Muscle Performance among the Elderly: A Meta-Analysis.
sources.text: There is increasing evidence showing the role of fatty acids and their derived lipid intermediates in the regulation of skeletal muscle mass synthesis and function. However, the role of omega-3 fatty acids remains unclear. Therefore, we conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate the potential effects of omega-3 fatty acids on sarcopenia-related performances among the elderly. Eligible literature and reports of randomized controlled trials were comprehensively searched from the PubMed, Cochrane Library, ClinicalTrials.gov, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL) databases until July 2018. A total of 10 articles were available for the meta-analysis. There were minor benefits for muscle mass gain (0.33 kg; 95% CI: 0.05, 0.62) and timed up and go performance (-0.30 s; 95% CI: -0.43, -0.17). Subgroup analyses regarding muscle mass and walk speed indicated that omega-3 fatty acid supplements at more than 2 g/day may contribute to muscle mass gain (0.67 kg; 95% CI: 0.16, 1.18) and improve walking speed, especially for those receiving more than 6 months of intervention (1.78 m/sec; 95% CI: 1.38, 2.17). Our findings provide some insight into the effects of omega-3 fatty acids on muscle mass, especially for those taking supplements at more than 2 g/day. We also observed that a long period of omega-3 fatty acids supplementation may improve walking speed.

sources.text: 65세 이상 어르신 권고: 일주일에 중간 강도 유산소 신체활동 150~300분 이상, 또는 고강도 75~150분 이상. 중간 강도 이상의 근력 운동을 일주일에 2일 이상. 기능적 균형과 근력을 강조한 복합 신체활동을 일주일에 3일 이상(기능을 높이고 낙상을 막기 위해). 앉아 있는 시간을 줄이고 어떤 강도든 신체활동으로 바꾸는 것이 건강에 이롭다. 권고량을 채우지 못하더라도 조금이라도 하는 것이 아무것도 하지 않는 것보다 낫다.
